Relative scale: the mother cow stands five-sixths the height of the father bull, the calf stands half the father's height, and the largest rainforest tree trunk stands three times the father's height. The father bull is a 12cm tall faceted quadruped of creamy off-white cold-press cardstock with dark umber ink patches on the flank, four folded rectangular pillar legs, a boxy scored head with glued black paper-dot eyes, and two massive swept crescent horns folded from scored pale terracotta kraft paper. The mother cow is a 10cm tall faceted quadruped of creamy off-white cardstock with dark umber ink flank markings, four folded pillar legs, a scored geometric head with black paper-dot eyes, and medium-length swept crescent horns of pale terracotta kraft paper. The calf is a 6cm tall faceted quadruped folded from warm beige cardstock with four slender folded strip legs, a scored wedge snout, black paper-dot eyes, and two tiny pointed pale terracotta horn nubs. World elements: static faceted rainforest tree trunks of damp bark brown kraft paper, low angular tufts of scored paper grass, and rigid faceted canopy leaves in jungle green and moss green. Palette strictly limited to creamy off-white, pale terracotta, warm beige, dark umber, jungle green, moss green, and damp bark brown. Lighting: single locked warm tungsten key light from upper-left raking across textured paper tooth and scored fold ridges, with faint cool fill from lower-right.
